subject: Agriculture
title: Urban Agriculture
description: A fast breakdown of Urban Agriculture for builders.

hook.text: Havana grows 90% of its fresh produce within city limits. Necessity drove Cuba to become an urban farming pioneer.

buildup.text: When Soviet aid collapsed in 1991, Cuba lost access to fuel, fertilizer, and food imports overnight.

discovery.text: Urban farms—called organoponicos—sprang up in vacant lots, using organic methods and providing neighborhood food security.

twist.text: Urban farming can't replace rural agriculture for staples. It works for vegetables, herbs, and local food access.

climax.text: Cities worldwide are adopting urban agriculture—rooftop farms, community gardens, and vertical systems.

punchline.text: Cities that grow food are more resilient. Cuba proved it under the worst conditions.

quiz.question: What percentage of Havana's fresh produce is grown within city limits?

details.summary: Urban agriculture grows food within and around cities using rooftops, vacant lots, vertical farms, and community gardens. This topic covers the scale, benefits, and limitations of urban food production as cities seek greater food resilience and green space.
details.whyItMatters: With 68% of the world's population expected to live in cities by 2050, urban agriculture offers communities a way to improve food access, reduce food miles, and build social cohesion.
takeaways: An estimated 800 million people worldwide practice some form of urban agriculture
Urban farms provide fresh produce to food deserts where grocery stores are scarce
City farming creates green jobs and repurposes vacant lots into productive community spaces

faq.question: What is urban agriculture and how significant is it?
faq.answer: Urban agriculture is food production within or near cities, including community gardens, rooftop farms, vertical indoor farms, and peri-urban plots. About 800 million people practice it globally, supplying up to 20% of food in some developing world cities.

faq.question: Can urban farming significantly contribute to food security?
faq.answer: Urban agriculture supplements food supply with fresh produce, improves nutrition in food deserts, and builds community resilience. However, it cannot replace rural agriculture for staple crops due to space, scale, and cost limitations.
